headline: Five majors above their 200-day line, but exchanges are seeing coin arrive, not leave
paragraphs: Five of the seven names on the board sit above their 200-day average: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB are all in that camp, while DOGE and ADA sit below it. That's a majority-bullish regime by trend, but it's not unanimous, and the two laggards are notable: DOGE is down 71.4% from its 12-month high and ADA is down 78.7% from its own, both still carrying the scars of a much deeper drawdown than the majors. ETH's above-200 status even comes with a golden cross flagged in the data, the kind of structural trend confirmation that matters more than a daily print.

Momentum is where the story gets interesting. BTC, ETH and SOL all carry RSI-14 in the high 60s (67.7, 67.3, 67.1), which is warm but not extreme, and BTC and SOL both show MACD above signal, meaning the trend-following momentum indicator agrees with the recent push higher. ETH is the outlier: RSI at 67.3 says momentum is still strong, but MACD is below signal, a divergence worth naming, price and RSI look constructive while the MACD histogram is telling a quieter story underneath. XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA all show MACD below signal too, and their RSI readings (62.0, 63.5, 54.7, 51.0) are cooler, consistent with assets that ran hard over the month (BNB +20.2%, XRP +23.9%) but have gone flat to negative on the week (XRP -5.9%, BNB -1.4%, DOGE -10.0%, ADA -12.2%). Every asset on this board shows day, week and month windows pointing in different directions, so scoping matters: BTC is down 0.8% on the day, up 1.1% on the week, and up 19.5% on the month, three different pictures depending on where you stand.

Positioning is mixed by asset. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0059% per 8 hours (6.4% annualized), a modest cost for longs, paired with a long/short ratio of 1.24, tilted long but not crowded. ETH funding is similar at 7.6% annualized with a 1.29 ratio. XRP and DOGE tell a louder story: XRP's long/short ratio is 2.45 with funding at 11.0% annualized, and DOGE's ratio is a striking 4.07 with a 9-hour liquidation window showing $393,826 in long liquidations against just $7,228 in shorts, that's a crowded long trade getting flushed. SOL stands apart with negative funding (-13.6% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their position, an unusual setup for an asset up 31.4% on the month with RSI at 67.1, momentum and positioning aren't agreeing there.

The flow picture adds tension. Over the last 24 hours, $126.2 million moved onto exchanges on net (the whale flow board's own framing), with ETH accounting for $109.0 million of that and BTC a smaller $17.3 million, both flagged as net moving onto exchanges. Zooming out, the last four weekly readings (week ending Aug 11 through Sep 01) all show net flow onto exchanges, ranging from $343 million to $924 million, so this isn't a one-day blip, it's a sustained multi-week pattern of coin arriving at exchanges rather than leaving. That sits awkwardly next to the ETF tape: BTC ETFs took in $216.7 million on 31 Aug, with a 5-session net of $803.6 million, and ETH ETFs pulled in $87.6 million on the same day with a 5-session net of $787.7 million and 10 straight days in the same direction. So traditional-finance flow into the ETFs is running positive at the same time coins are net moving onto exchanges, two different channels of the market pointing different ways, worth sitting with rather than resolving.

Stablecoin float is up 1.11% over 30 days to $308.9 billion, a modest build in dry powder rather than a surge. Sentiment, meanwhile, reads 69, Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 25 to 74. That's a crowd feeling good while the exchange-flow data shows coin moving toward, not away from, the venues where it gets sold. When the gauge and the tape disagree like this, the disagreement itself is the signal worth watching, not either side alone.

What to watch from here: whether the onto-exchanges trend breaks its weekly pattern (four straight weeks running the same way is a real streak; a flip to net outflows would matter), whether ETH's MACD-below-signal divergence resolves by momentum fading or by MACD catching up, and whether DOGE's crowded long positioning (4.07 long/short ratio) produces further liquidation events on the short side of that ledger. A funding flip on SOL from negative back to positive would also mark a change in who's paying whom to hold the bet.
